note: Six hand-built, hand-traced cases comparing IFEval's word count (re.findall(r'\w+')) with a whitespace split, and the length_constraints:number_words verdict under each. expected_* fields are fixed before the sealed run (see prereg.md). Every case is a minimal, self-contained string; none require any model or network.

cases.value: I don't think we can't go now.
cases.mechanism: The apostrophe is not a word char, so \w+ splits each contraction: don't -> don, t and can't -> can, t. IFEval counts 9, a whitespace split counts 7; 'at least 8' passes under IFEval but fails under whitespace.
Hyphens and the decimal point are not word chars: state-of-the-art -> 4 tokens, 3.5 -> 3, 5. IFEval counts 9 vs 5 for a whitespace split; 'at least 6' flips.
Periods inside acronyms split them: U.S.A. -> U, S, A and U.K. -> U, K. IFEval counts 8 vs 5; 'less than 6' passes under a whitespace split but fails under IFEval.
Tokens with no word character (an emoji, '!!!', an em dash) are dropped by \w+ but kept by a whitespace split, so here IFEval UNDER-counts: 2 vs 6. 'at least 3' flips in the opposite direction.

cases.value: Set the max_retries value to five
cases.mechanism: Control: the underscore IS a word char, so max_retries stays one token under both counters. Counts agree (6 = 6) and no verdict flips -- not all text diverges.
Thousands separators split the number: 1,000,000 -> 1, 000, 000. IFEval counts 8 vs 6; 'at least 7' flips.
